skill.name: openserv-client
skill.description: Guide for using @openserv-labs/client to provision OpenServ agents, manage workflows, configure triggers, handle credentials, and use x402 and ERC-8004 features.
skill.summary: Use @openserv-labs/client to provision agents, manage OpenServ workflows, configure triggers, and handle platform authentication.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most command-execution and network alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, TypeScript template strings, and expected OpenServ endpoints. I confirmed substantive risks around wallet and API credential handling, local .env state, webhook trigger-token logging, and a destructive cleanup example. No prompt injection attempt or hidden host-level command execution was found.

remediation.issue: Webhook trigger tokens are printed in example logs.
remediation.suggestion: Redact trigger tokens by default and require explicit user action before printing full webhook URLs.

remediation.issue: Wallet private keys and API keys are loaded from .env and process.env.
remediation.suggestion: Document file permissions, .gitignore requirements, key rotation, and secret manager use for production deployments.

remediation.issue: The cleanup example can delete all workflows and agents.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run output, require a second confirmation for --all, and support scoped deletion by workspace or label.

remediation.issue: Setup examples handle API keys and auth tokens directly.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid printing credential prefixes and show redacted placeholders when explaining .env output.

content.value_statement: OpenServ agent deployment requires provisioning, credentials, workflows, and trigger configuration. This skill gives Codex, Claude, and Claude Code a focused OpenServ client reference.
actual_capabilities: Explains provision() setup for agent registration, workflow creation, triggers, and credential binding.
Documents PlatformClient methods for agents, workflows, triggers, tasks, integrations, models, payments, and web3.
Shows TypeScript examples for creating agents, activating workflows, and firing webhook or x402 triggers.
Covers environment variables for wallet and user API key authentication.
Describes ERC-8004 on-chain registration, wallet funding, and deployment state behavior.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for stuck tasks, sync issues, auth errors, and paywall fields.
limitations: It is documentation and examples, not an installed OpenServ runtime.
Examples require valid OpenServ credentials and network access to platform services.
OpenServ APIs may change after the bundled reference was authored.
Wallet and API key handling must be reviewed before production use.

use_cases.title: Prototype an OpenServ Agent
use_cases.description: Use the quick-start flow to plan provisioning, workflow creation, trigger setup, and local agent startup.

use_cases.title: Configure Paid Agent Access
use_cases.description: Map x402 trigger settings, input schemas, wallet requirements, and paywall behavior before publishing a paid workflow.

use_cases.title: Operate Platform Resources
use_cases.description: Use PlatformClient references to list, update, activate, debug, and clean up OpenServ agents and workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a webhook agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the openserv-client skill to outline a basic webhook agent setup. Include provisioning, credentials, workflow, trigger, and run sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare wallet and user API key usage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which OpenServ credential I should use for PlatformClient management calls. Cover wallet authentication, user API keys, and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Paid Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an x402 OpenServ workflow for a paid agent service. Include trigger fields, payout wallet requirements, timeout settings, and test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my OpenServ deployment plan for production readiness. Check provisioning, secret handling, trigger exposure, ERC-8004 registration, cleanup safety, and troubleshooting gaps.

output_examples.input: I need a webhook agent that receives a text request and returns an AI response.
output: A provisioning plan with agent name, workflow goal, webhook trigger, input field, and task description.
A credential checklist covering user API key, wallet private key, and local state files.
A run sequence for local testing before deployment.

output_examples.input: My ERC-8004 registration fails after provisioning.
output_examples.output: The answer explains wallet funding on Base, reloading environment variables after provisioning, chain ID checks, and safe retry behavior.

output_examples.input: I want to expose my agent as a paid API.
output_examples.output: The answer outlines x402 trigger configuration, input schema planning, payout wallet setup, timeout guidance, and manual payment testing.

best_practices: Call provision() before deployment so platform state and local credentials exist.
Use long timeouts for webhook and x402 triggers that run complex agent tasks.
Keep wallet private keys and OpenServ API keys out of source control and logs.
anti_patterns: Using the agent API key for PlatformClient management calls.
Publishing full webhook trigger URLs in public logs or documentation.
Clearing wallet state when you want to preserve the same ERC-8004 agent identity.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you use @openserv-labs/client to provision agents, workflows, triggers, payments, and platform resources.

faq.question: Does it replace the OpenServ agent SDK?
faq.answer: No. It complements the agent SDK, which defines and runs agent capabilities.

faq.question: Which credentials are covered?
faq.answer: It covers wallet private keys, OpenServ user API keys, agent API keys, and auth tokens.

faq.question: Can it help with x402 payments?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents x402 trigger setup, payment execution, payout wallets, and paywall behavior.

faq.question: Does it include ERC-8004 guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers on-chain registration, wallet funding, chain selection, and deployment state updates.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review secret storage, webhook token exposure, cleanup scripts, trigger timeouts, and current OpenServ API behavior.
